tldr: The equal-weight causal Jensen--Shannon detection frontier under complete randomization is \(\rho(N,K,m)=\max\{K/N,\sqrt K/m\}\), with sole crossover \(m\sqrt K=N\). One total original-record test has weak-null size at most \(1/20\) at every legal finite triple. At every triple with \(A_\dagger\rho<1/100\), alternatives at \(c\rho\) and \(C\rho\) are nonempty, its worst-case power at \(C\rho\) is at least \(1-24/C-36/4097>3/4\), and maximin power at \(c\rho\) is at most \(10/99<1/4\). The vanishing-separation theorem and the original rare-arm theorem are immediate corollaries. The donor is published explicit-reference iid identity testing; an exact observable split-and-reuse channel and uniform split-risk bounds prove its transfer to arbitrary-pairing causal tables. Lawful fixed-table priors give the converse for complete records.
